This file restates\nonly the rules an agent breaks most often, because each one has cost real CI\ntime ([issue #1191](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1191)).\n\n## The single push gate\n\nA push starts several workflows at once. Each push that only fixes part of the\nprevious run's failures pays for the whole matrix again. Pull request #1188\nneeded 100 commits and 11 `CI/CD Pipeline` runs, and none of them was green.\nThe rules below make every push count:\n\n1. **Drafting sub-agents never push.** A sub-agent that drafts code, tests or\n   documentation commits locally (or hands its diff back) and stops there.\n   Only the coordinating agent touches the remote.\n2. **One CI/CD agent pushes, once per round.** Exactly one agent owns pushes to\n   the branch. It pushes only after it has collected every actionable failure\n   of the latest run on the current head, and fixed all of them in the same\n   batch.\n3. **Never push while a run is in progress on the branch.** Check first:\n\n   ```bash\n   gh run list --branch \"$(git branch --show-current)\" --status in_progress --json databaseId,workflowName\n   gh run list --branch \"$(git branch --show-current)\" --status queued --json databaseId,workflowName\n   ```\n\n   Both lists must be empty, or must hold only runs for an older head that you\n   are deliberately superseding. Otherwise, keep drafting while the run\n   finishes, then collect its failures (rule 2).\n4. **Run the JavaScript checks locally before the push.** Two kinds of check\n   apply:\n   - the test files next to the change, run one at a time:\n     `timeout 600 node --test --test-concurrency=1 <file>`;\n   - the gates the change touches. These run in JavaScript and never compile\n     Rust: `node experiments/formal_ai_subagent/local-gates.mjs --only <gate>`.\n\n   `--list` shows every gate. Run the whole set\n   (`node experiments/formal_ai_subagent/local-gates.mjs`) before a push that\n   touches shared data such as `data/meta`. The fast pull-request lane runs the\n   same twins, so a failure here would have failed there too.\n5. **No full local Rust build unless the change is Rust-only.** CI compiles\n   Rust: the focused `native-type-check` job on pull requests, and the full\n   matrix on main. Locally, run `rustfmt --check <file>` on the files you\n   changed. That command needs no build.\n6. **If a change is Rust-only and you must build locally, keep the build\n   bounded.** Use one shared target directory for every worktree and agent,\n   with no incremental cache, few jobs, and a prune afterwards:\n\n   ```bash\n   export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=\"$HOME/.cache/formal-ai-target\"  # one directory, shared by all worktrees\n   export CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0                               # no incremental cache to grow without bound\n   export CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2                                # a limited -j for plain cargo commands\n   CARGO_TEST_JOBS=2 scripts/cargo-test.sh --test unit <filter>  # one module, -j 2, then prunes\n   scripts/prune-build-cache.sh                             # prunes old artifacts after any other cargo command\n   ```\n\n   `scripts/prune-build-cache.sh` follows `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. It keeps only\n   the latest build's artifacts, and by default it caps the tree at 4 GB\n   locally (`CARGO_TARGET_MAX_SIZE_MB`).\n\n## Where things live\n\n- Production-only failures are recorded in\n  [`data/meta/main-only-regressions.lino`](data/meta/main-only-regressions.lino).\n  These are failures that main recorded after a green pull request. When main\n  fails after a green pull request, add the failure there together with the\n  narrowest pre-merge check that replays it.\n- The fast pull-request JavaScript inventory is\n  [`data/benchmarks/fast-pull-request-javascript-tests.json`](data/benchmarks/fast-pull-request-javascript-tests.json).\n- Runner labels are pinned, and `node scripts/check-runner-labels.mjs` rejects\n  `-latest` labels.\n- Experiments go in `./experiments`. There is no top-level `examples/`\n  directory; Rust examples live in `rust/examples/`.\n- Never commit agent scratch state such as `.claude/`.",

[2026-11-25T00:02:50.509Z] [INFO]         "content": "> ## Documentation Index\n> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://code.claude.com/docs/llms.txt\n> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.\n\n# Auto mode classifier request charges\n\n> Resolve the Claude Code notice saying this session isn't eligible for auto mode's no-charge classifier requests: what it means, why it appears, and what to do.\n\nIn [auto mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes.md#eliminate-prompts-with-auto-mode), a classifier checks actions such as shell commands and network requests before they run. Wherever [server-side checks are on](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes.md#server-side-classifier-review), the server performs those checks as part of the session's own model requests, at no charge. This notice means the server's checks aren't reaching your session, so Claude Code is making its own classifier requests instead, and on your account those requests count toward your token usage:\n\n```text theme={null}\nWe're changing auto mode to no longer charge for classifier requests in Claude Code. However, this session isn't eligible.\n```\n\nAt the prompt, Claude Code holds the first action it would check that way until you answer. Auto mode keeps working, and its classifier requests are billed as they were before.\n\nThe most common cause is an LLM gateway or proxy between Claude Code and the API, and when Claude Code can identify one, the notice names it. Press **Enter** to continue, or see [Make the session eligible](#make-the-session-eligible) to keep it from appearing in new sessions.\n\n## Respond to the notice\n\nThe notice holds the action until you answer it:\n\n* **Enter** continues: the held action and the rest of the session use Claude Code's own classifier requests, billed as token usage as before, and the notice doesn't appear again in that session. When the notice named a gateway, acknowledging it keeps it from reappearing on this machine for 24 hours. When it didn't, the notice returns the next time a session falls back.\n* **Esc** or **Ctrl+C** cancels: the held action doesn't run and the current turn stops, with the session still in auto mode. Nothing is remembered, so the notice appears again before the next checked action.\n\nTo stop using auto mode instead, switch permission modes with `Shift+Tab` after you answer.\n\nWhere the notice can't wait for an answer, Claude Code reports the same text and the session continues in auto mode, unless a gateway acknowledgment on this machine in the last 24 hours has dismissed it. In [non-interactive mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless.md) with `-p` it prints the text to stderr, and in `stream-json` output it emits a `system` warning message, which Agent SDK applications can read from the message stream.\n\n## Make the session eligible\n\nIf a gateway keeps auto mode's server-side checks from reaching your sessions and you don't run it, send the requirements below to your company's admin or your gateway provider. Where [the upstream accepts the format that the gateway receives](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-protocol.md#format-mismatch-with-the-upstream), Claude Code expects the gateway to pass requests and responses through unchanged, as the [gateway compatibility guide](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-protocol.md#feature-pass-through) describes:\n\n* **Requests**: to let the checks through, the gateway forwards both the `anthropic-beta` header and the `safeguards` body field unchanged, because [the two travel as a pair](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-protocol.md#beta-header-and-body-field-pairs). On the [Amazon Bedrock InvokeModel format](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-protocol.md#api-formats), it forwards the `anthropic_beta` body field in place of the header.\n* **Responses**: the gateway returns responses and streaming events without dropping fields or rewriting tool-use IDs. To let the checks' results through, it keeps the `safeguard_results` field.\n\nOnce your gateway does this, new sessions use the server's checks again.\n\nIf you already know that your gateway can't provide the server's checks, tell Claude Code not to ask for them there by setting `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_SERVER` to `0` before you start the session, in your shell or in the [`env` settings key](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#env):\n\n```bash theme={null}\nexport CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_SERVER=0\n```\n\nClassifier requests are then always Claude Code's own, billed the same way, and the notice doesn't appear. On a direct connection to the Anthropic API, the variable requires Claude Code v2.1.281 or later. Setting `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS=1` while `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_SERVER` is unset turns the server's checks off as well, except as [Disable pre-release capabilities](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-protocol.md#disable-pre-release-capabilities) describes.\n\n`CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_SERVER` is a temporary setting and may be removed in a later release.\n\n## Why the notice appears\n\nOn a Pro, Max, Ultra, or Team plan, you never see the notice. To find out which sessions ask the server for the classifier checks, see [Server-side classifier review](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes.md#server-side-classifier-review). If you see the notice, check for these usual causes:\n\n* **An LLM gateway or proxy is in the path**: one that strips or rewrites request headers, drops request fields it doesn't recognize, or edits responses. The server then never receives the request for checks, or Claude Code never receives the results. When your configuration or the responses identify the gateway, the notice names it.\n* **Server-side checks haven't reached your platform, region, or credential yet**: whether a platform or region performs them depends on that platform's rollout. If you see the notice with no gateway or proxy in the path and it keeps appearing, this is the likely cause. To confirm, contact support or your company's admin, or report it with `/feedback`.\n\nTo check a session that's in auto mode, run `/status` at the Claude Code prompt: its **Auto mode server** row reads `Enabled` while the server's checks decide the session's actions and `Disabled` once the session has fallen back.\n\nWhen a gateway cuts responses short or rewrites the results into a form Claude Code can't read, you get denials with no verdict in place of this notice; see [Server-side classifier review](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes.md#server-side-classifier-review).\n\n## Related resources\n\n* [Auto mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes.md#eliminate-prompts-with-auto-mode): what auto mode is and what it blocks by default\n* [Server-side classifier review](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes.md#server-side-classifier-review): which sessions ask the server to check actions, and the Claude Code version each one requires\n* [Gateway compatibility guide](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-protocol.md#feature-pass-through): what breaks when a gateway strips headers or body fields\n* [The server returned no safety verdict](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors.md#the-server-returned-no-safety-verdict): the denial you see when the server gives no verdict for an action\n* [Manage costs effectively](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs.md): track token usage and reduce Claude Code costs\n"

When it didn't, the notice returns the next time a session falls back.\n* **Esc** or **Ctrl+C** cancels: the held action doesn't run and the current turn stops, with the session still in auto mode. Nothing is remembered, so the notice appears again before the next checked action.\n\nTo stop using auto mode instead, switch permission modes with `Shift+Tab` after you answer.\n\nWhere the notice can't wait for an answer, Claude Code reports the same text and the session continues in auto mode, unless a gateway acknowledgment on this machine in the last 24 hours has dismissed it. In [non-interactive mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless.md) with `-p` it prints the text to stderr, and in `stream-json` output it emits a `system` warning message, which Agent SDK applications can read from the message stream.\n\n## Make the session eligible\n\nIf a gateway keeps auto mode's server-side checks from reaching your sessions and you don't run it, send the requirements below to your company's admin or your gateway provider. Where [the upstream accepts the format that the gateway receives](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-protocol.md#format-mismatch-with-the-upstream), Claude Code expects the gateway to pass requests and responses through unchanged, as the [gateway compatibility guide](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-protocol.md#feature-pass-through) describes:\n\n* **Requests**: to let the checks through, the gateway forwards both the `anthropic-beta` header and the `safeguards` body field unchanged, because [the two travel as a pair](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-protocol.md#beta-header-and-body-field-pairs). On the [Amazon Bedrock InvokeModel format](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-protocol.md#api-formats), it forwards the `anthropic_beta` body field in place of the header.\n* **Responses**: the gateway returns responses and streaming events without dropping fields or rewriting tool-use IDs. To let the checks' results through, it keeps the `safeguard_results` field.\n\nOnce your gateway does this, new sessions use the server's checks again.\n\nIf you already know that your gateway can't provide the server's checks, tell Claude Code not to ask for them there by setting `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_SERVER` to `0` before you start the session, in your shell or in the [`env` settings key](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#env):\n\n```bash theme={null}\nexport CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_SERVER=0\n```\n\nClassifier requests are then always Claude Code's own, billed the same way, and the notice doesn't appear. On a direct connection to the Anthropic API, the variable requires Claude Code v2.1.281 or later. Setting `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS=1` while `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_SERVER` is unset turns the server's checks off as well, except as [Disable pre-release capabilities](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-protocol.md#disable-pre-release-capabilities) describes.\n\n`CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_SERVER` is a temporary setting and may be removed in a later release.\n\n## Why the notice appears\n\nOn a Pro, Max, Ultra, or Team plan, you never see the notice. To find out which sessions ask the server for the classifier checks, see [Server-side classifier review](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes.md#server-side-classifier-review). If you see the notice, check for these usual causes:\n\n* **An LLM gateway or proxy is in the path**: one that strips or rewrites request headers, drops request fields it doesn't recognize, or edits responses. The server then never receives the request for checks, or Claude Code never receives the results. When your configuration or the responses identify the gateway, the notice names it.\n* **Server-side checks haven't reached your platform, region, or credential yet**: whether a platform or region performs them depends on that platform's rollout. If you see the notice with no gateway or proxy in the path and it keeps appearing, this is the likely cause. To confirm, contact support or your company's admin, or report it with `/feedback`.\n\nTo check a session that's in auto mode, run `/status` at the Claude Code prompt: its **Auto mode server** row reads `Enabled` while the server's checks decide the session's actions and `Disabled` once the session has fallen back.\n\nWhen a gateway cuts responses short or rewrites the results into a form Claude Code can't read, you get denials with no verdict in place of this notice; see [Server-side classifier review](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes.md#server-side-classifier-review).\n\n## Related resources\n\n* [Auto mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes.md#eliminate-prompts-with-auto-mode): what auto mode is and what it blocks by default\n* [Server-side classifier review](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes.md#server-side-classifier-review): which sessions ask the server to check actions, and the Claude Code version each one requires\n* [Gateway compatibility guide](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-protocol.md#feature-pass-through): what breaks when a gateway strips headers or body fields\n* [The server returned no safety verdict](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors.md#the-server-returned-no-safety-verdict): the denial you see when the server gives no verdict for an action\n* [Manage costs effectively](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs.md): track token usage and reduce Claude Code costs\n",

.find(|node| node.name == \"auto_mode_classifier\")\n        .expect(\"data/seed/auto-mode-classifier.lino must declare auto_mode_classifier\");\n    let values = |name: &str| -> Vec<String> {\n ClassifierRule {\n    let patterns = node\n        .children\n        .iter()\n        .filter(|child| child.name == \"pattern\")\n        .map(|child| {\n            RegexBuilder::new(&child.id)\n child.id)\n                })\n        })\n        .collect();\n    ClassifierRule {\n        name: node.id.clone(),\n        reason: node.find_child_value(\"reason\").to_owned(),\n        patterns,\n   !self.markers.is_empty() && self.markers.iter().all(|marker| system.contains(marker))\n    }\n\n    /// The agent actions inside the request's `<transcript>`: every JSON line\n    /// whose key is not the user entry key, decoded to its string values.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn agent_actions(&self, messages: &str) -> Vec<String> {\n        let transcript = messages\n        ),\n                },\n            )\n    }\n\n    fn allow(&self) -> ClassifierVerdict {\n        ClassifierVerdict {\n            blocked_by: None,\n            text: self.allow_text.clone(),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Judge a classifier request given its system and message text; `None` when\n/// the request is not an auto-mode classifier .then(|| policy.judge(messages))\n}\n\n/// Cut a verdict at the first requested stop sequence, the way the Anthropic\n/// API does: the text before the stop sequence is returned and the matched\n/// The user's own messages are never checked against these rules.\n- **R5, multi-select:** the \"where to send the report\" question is now multi-select in Claude, and every chosen destination runs. Codex 0.166 has no multi-select option and only asks questions in Plan mode; its answers were already handled correctly.\n- **R6, error reporting:** \"Отправь отчёт об ошибке\" is now recognized as a report request instead of a research question. \"Отправь письмо маме\" is still treated as an ordinary request.\n- **R7, case study:** written in `docs/case-studies/issue-1632/README.md`.\n\nOne gap in testing: the new Rust unit tests for the auto-mode check and the how-to answers have not been run anywhere yet. They compile (`cargo check --lib --tests` passed), but building the test binary ran out of memory in this sandbox. This PR's CI doesn't run them either; they only run in `release.yml` after merging to main. The JavaScript versions of the same tests pass locally, and the Rust integration tests pass in CI. The PR description says this."

Codex 0.166 has no multi-select option and only asks questions in Plan mode; its answers were already handled correctly.\n- **R6, error reporting:** \"Отправь отчёт об ошибке\" is now recognized as a report request instead of a research question. \"Отправь письмо маме\" is still treated as an ordinary request.\n- **R7, case study:** written in `docs/case-studies/issue-1632/README.md`.\n\nOne gap in testing: the new Rust unit tests for the auto-mode check and the how-to answers have not been run anywhere yet. They compile (`cargo check --lib --tests` passed), but building the test binary ran out of memory in this sandbox. This PR's CI doesn't run them either; they only run in `release.yml` after merging to main. The JavaScript versions of the same tests pass locally, and the Rust integration tests pass in CI. This PR covers the November 24 follow-up comment: `formal-ai with claude` could not answer `Как какать?`, listed unused sources, treated \"Отправь отчёт об ошибке\" as a research question, asked a single-choice \"Select one or more\" question, and refused every Bash call in auto mode.\n\n| # | Requirement | Fix |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R1 | Every \"how to X?\" question goes to wikiHow first | wikiHow is always probed, even when a past timeout or 429 is cached as \"unreachable\" for 7 days.
